links.comparator_used: Outputs across the different input education levels (6th grade, 8th grade, high school, bachelor's) for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, scored against target readability; no single fixed-output arm
links.outcome: Readability (FKRE and FKGL) of LLM output compared with the prespecified patient education level
links.effect: GPT-3.5 FKGL means were 9.08, 10.27, 13.4 and 13.74 for 6th grade, 8th grade, high school and bachelor's, and it aligned with the target only at the bachelor's level. GPT-4 FKGL means were 6.3, 6.7, 11.09 and 17.03 and it met the target for all groups except the 6th-grade FKRE average. Both models showed significant differences in FKRE and FKGL across education levels (P<.001 for most comparisons).
links.tradeoff: Output readability fell into 3 broad tiers (easy, medium, difficult) rather than 4 distinct levels. GPT-3.5 largely failed to reach the lower-grade targets, and GPT-4 missed the 6th-grade FKRE target.
links.quote: GLMs can change the structure and readability of medical text outputs according to input-specified education.

design_hint: reading-level constraints in prompts (tailoring output to patient education level)
